clue.text: Trampled by mount, duke has to struggle out of action

indicators.note: something trampled lies beneath a horse's body, so the duke's letter is set within the mount's letters

parts.note: a mount is a horse that is ridden
a struggle or fight is combat

explanation.surface: A duke is knocked out of the fight after being trampled by his own horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trampled by' is a container signal here: the duke ends up under the horse. 'has to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally 'outside the fight', is used in English for anyone disabled or no longer able to take part.

clue.text: Damaging number of fish caught nets marine fine

indicators.note: to net is to catch, so the catch surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: a haul is a catch of fish
RM stands for Royal Marine(s)
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A trawler's catch is damaging when it nets a fine marine creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nets' looks like the plural noun of the fishing scene but works as a verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmful means causing harm, i.e. damaging.

clue.text: Play with two characters on the radio

definitions.text: Play with two characters on the radio

parts.words: Play with two characters on the radio
parts.note: seems to be a two-hander broadcast drama; in fact the play's title is two words of the radio phonetic alphabet joined by 'and', both also its title characters

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy is named after two lovers whose names are also radio alphabet code words for R and J.

clue.text: Stop running Derby regularly as the jockeys are going

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the race's name

parts.note: jockeys riding in a race are said to be up

explanation.surface: The Derby is regularly stopped while the jockeys are heading out.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of Derby give DRY. The Derby is a famous English flat race.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry up is to stop flowing, as a spring or supply runs dry.

clue.text: What's put on wall once past courses

definitions.text: What's put on wall once past courses

parts.words: What's put on wall once past courses
parts.note: courses here are the layers of bricks; once the builder is past them, a topping stone goes on

explanation.definitionFit: A capstone is the stone that tops and finishes a wall, laid on above the final course.

clue.text: Insect now initially flying in May?

indicators.note: flying means departing, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: May is an example of a month, hence the question mark

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An insect is now flying about in May.
explanation.walkthrough: MONTH loses N to give the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A moth is a mainly night-flying insect related to the butterfly.

clue.text: Saint's thirty-one days in ecstasy

parts.note: August is a month of thirty-one days
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A holy man spends a month in rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustine of Hippo is a celebrated Christian saint and theologian.

clue.text: Who might show a sort of elitist leaning?

definitions.text: Who might show a sort of elitist leaning?

indicators.note: a sort of means a version of, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks which group might display snobbish tendencies.
explanation.walkthrough: ELITIST LEANING has exactly the fourteen letters; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are the educated intellectual class, often accused of elitism.

clue.text: One dying for the faith to damage pagan god

parts.note: to mar is to damage
Tyr is the Norse god of war

explanation.surface: A believer dies for refusing to honour a heathen deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone killed for their religious beliefs.

clue.text: Expression of surprise following odd game

indicators.note: the exclamation comes after the word for odd, so it is placed second

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or strange
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise after a strange game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is a card game in which players collect sets and runs.

clue.text: Craggy region that might give a goat pain

indicators.note: the region's name, rearranged, might yield the following words, so they are letters to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A rough mountainous place sounds hard going even for a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text repeated 'a'; the page prints it once. The nine letters of A GOAT PAIN rearrange into the region's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia, at the southern tip of South America, is a famously rugged, mountainous region.

clue.text: Highwayman wanting diamonds takes much from the cross-country route

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the card-suit letter is removed from the robber

parts.note: a footpad was a highway robber who went on foot
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

indicators.note: taking most of the little word means dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: A robber without his jewels steals from walkers on a country track.
explanation.walkthrough: FOOTPAD less D gives FOOTPA; 'much from the' gives TH; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpath is a path for walkers, often running across country.

clue.text: Spoken agreement made by Hilary and Tenzing

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so the word for agreement is heard rather than written

parts.note: assent is agreement or consent

explanation.surface: Two famous mountaineers verbally agree on something.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Hillary (spelt Hilary here) and Tenzing Norgay made the first climb of Everest in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing Hillary and Tenzing achieved in 1953 was the first climb up Everest.

clue.text: Protracted applause for script

parts.note: protracted means drawn out, long
to give someone a hand is to applaud them

explanation.surface: Lengthy clapping greets a screenplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Longhand is ordinary handwriting, as opposed to shorthand or type, i.e. a script.

clue.text: River in old Bath turned out an apt place to live

indicators.note: in places the river's letters inside the others
turned out means rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A river near Bath has an old dwelling turned out of it, fit for living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges old plus Bath; the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and others in England). 'apt' hints at a fitting home on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseboat is a boat fitted as a home, apt for living on a river.

clue.text: Dusty food processor has millions comparatively unwell

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)
the comparative of ill is iller

explanation.surface: A grubby kitchen gadget is worth millions but in poorer shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food processor' suggests a kitchen gadget; it is a person who grinds grain, dusty from the flour.
explanation.definitionFit: A miller grinds grain into flour and is traditionally covered in flour dust.

clue.text: They don't think American car needs German agent? Not half!

parts.note: auto is American for a car

indicators.note: only half of the spy's name is kept

parts.note: Mata Hari spied for Germany in the First World War

explanation.surface: A US car is a German spy's choice, emphatically so.
explanation.walkthrough: MATA HARI halved leaves MATA; 'needs' is a link and 'Not half!' also reads as British slang for 'very much'.
explanation.definitionFit: Automata are robots or self-operating machines, which go through motions without thought.

clue.text: Shock over place for Hindu caste member

indicators.note: over signals turning the word back to front

parts.note: to jar is to jolt or shock
to put is to place

explanation.surface: Being placed in a particular caste comes as a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the shock word round; the Raj also recalls British rule in India, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Rajputs are members of a Hindu warrior caste of northern India.

clue.text: Kitchener's instructions concerning writing up of heroic work

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing up means the word runs from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: an epic is a heroic poem

explanation.surface: Lord Kitchener's orders concern writing up an epic campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener suggests the British field marshal; here it is a cook, one who works in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions for a cook preparing a dish.

clue.text: A universal author's written about good area of France

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: the author is set around the letter for good

parts.note: Jules Verne is the French author; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A writer of universal appeal has written about a fine French region.
explanation.walkthrough: G sits inside VERNE to make VERGNE, after A and U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Auvergne is a mountainous region of south-central France.

clue.text: Came to maturity: it's all up with the last bit of selfish behaviour

indicators.text: it's all up with the last bit
indicators.note: in a down clue the final letter goes up to the top

parts.note: got ripe means matured

explanation.surface: Once grown up, a person's self-absorption is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: GOT RIPE's final E rises to the top. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an act done for self-gratification, a selfish indulgence.

clue.text: Young horse traps half of left band round shaft

indicators.note: to trap is to hold inside, so the horse's letters surround the half-word

parts.note: a colt is a young male horse

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word means its first two letters

explanation.surface: A foal gets caught up in a strap left round a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of left' takes its first two letters; 'traps' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A collet is a collar or ring that grips round a shaft or spindle.

clue.text: Newly-built resort on site south of Naples

indicators.note: something newly built is put together afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new holiday resort is built on a site near Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrento is a coastal town on the bay just south of Naples.

clue.text: Quick attack seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means holding, so the attack surrounds the letter

parts.note: a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: A swift raid takes control.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast or quick.

clue.text: Vessel for claret wine filled with ultimate in Bourgogne

indicators.note: the wine word is filled with the next letter

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: ultimate in means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A claret jug filled with Burgundy.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is old slang for blood; Bourgogne is French for Burgundy.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a blood vessel, carrying blood ('claret' in old slang).

clue.text: In public house, no end of cash returned to woman: strange doings!

indicators.note: returned means turned back, so the trimmed word is read backwards
with no end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: cash is money
Ena is a woman's name, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: In a pub, someone hands a woman her money back, and odd things happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' trims the cash word and 'returned' turns it back; Ena is a stock crossword woman. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable events or occurrences, the strange happenings of the definition.

clue.text: What's difficult subject for an artist?

definitions.meaning: someone who sits or stands for a painter

explanation.definitionFit: A poser is both a tricky question and a person who models for a painter.

clue.text: Slender structure offering light support

parts.note: light support reads as minor help, but it is a tall thin household object that holds a lamp bulb up high

explanation.definitionFit: A tall floor lamp on a slender pole literally supports a light.
